questions.prompt: A food is rubbed on paper and leaves an oily, see-through patch. What does it contain?
Plan how you would test whether a sample of dhokla contains starch, including a control.
questions.modelAnswer: Crush a small piece of dhokla with a little water in a test tube. Add two or three drops of dilute iodine solution and observe the colour. As a control, add the same amount of iodine to a tube of plain water (stays brown) and, for comparison, to a known starch source like boiled rice (turns blue-black). If the dhokla turns blue-black, it contains starch. Handle iodine carefully because it stains.
rubric: Add iodine and note the colour
questions.explain: Criterion B: a clear, controlled test.

questions.text: In the protein test, copper sulphate and sodium hydroxide turn ___ if protein is present.
questions.explain: The colour changes from blue to violet.
